toc.title: File storage, hybrid, backup and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EBS: Elastic Block Store; EFS: Elastic File System; AZ: Availability Zone; IA: Infrequent Access; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; SSD: solid state drive; HDD: hard disk drive; KMS: Key Management Service; NFS: Network File System; ECS: Elastic Container Service; EKS: Elastic Kubernetes Service; SMB: Server Message Block; RDS: Relational Database Service

  • Tell object, block and file storage apart, and match each to an AWS service
  • Choose the right Amazon S3 storage class, from Standard to Glacier Deep Archive
  • Explain S3 Lifecycle rules and S3 Versioning
  • Compare Amazon EBS and instance store, and Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx
  • Place AWS Storage Gateway, AWS Backup and AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery

2Object and block storage

Running case

Tidewater's Data Grows

  • Customers upload millions of product photos, which few people view after the sale
  • Order records must be kept for years at the lowest cost
  • The shop's database server needs a fast disk, and the Linux web servers must share one set of files
  • The warehouse office keeps files on site but wants cloud storage behind them
  • The founder wants consistent backups and a quick recovery if a server room is lost
  • Your job: choose the right storage for each need

Object, Block and File Storage

  • Object storage keeps objects (a file plus metadata) in buckets: Amazon S3
  • Block storage gives a virtual disk to a server: Amazon EBS and instance store
  • File storage gives a shared file system many servers can mount: Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx
  • Archive and backup services sit on top: S3 Glacier classes, AWS Backup, Elastic Disaster Recovery
  • Hybrid access from your own data center: AWS Storage Gateway

Exam tip

Name the type first: objects, a disk for one server, or a shared file system.

Amazon S3: Object Storage at Any Scale

  • Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is object storage: you store any amount of data as objects in buckets
  • Uses include websites, backup and restore, archives, data lakes and mobile apps
  • An object is a file plus metadata, found by its key (name) inside a bucket
  • You choose the Region for a bucket; objects never leave that Region unless you move or replicate them
  • Buckets and objects are private by default, and Block Public Access is on by default
  • You pay only for what you use, with no overage charges
  • Reads after writes are strongly consistent
Exam tip

Unlimited, durable, internet-scale storage for files and media: Amazon S3.

S3 Storage Classes: Frequent and Infrequent Access [Verify live]

Class Use it for Notes
S3 Standard Frequently accessed data, millisecond access; the default Three or more AZs
S3 Intelligent-Tiering Unknown or changing access patterns Moves objects between tiers automatically; no retrieval fees
S3 Standard-IA Long-lived, infrequently accessed data, millisecond access 30-day minimum, retrieval fee
S3 One Zone-IA Re-creatable, infrequently accessed data One AZ; lost if that AZ is lost
S3 Express One Zone Single-digit millisecond access, one chosen AZ Beyond the guide Latency-sensitive apps
  • Every class listed is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability
  • As of 4 November 2026: figures are from the S3 User Guide
Exam tip

Unknown pattern: Intelligent-Tiering. Re-creatable and cheaper: One Zone-IA.

S3 Glacier Classes: Archive Storage Old name [Verify live]

Class Use it for Notes
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval Rarely accessed archives, read about once a quarter, with millisecond access 90-day minimum
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval Archives read about once a year; retrieval in minutes to hours 90-day minimum; restore first
S3 Glacier Deep Archive Lowest-cost archive read less than once a year; retrieval in hours 180-day minimum; restore first
  • Retrieval fees apply to all three
  • The older Amazon Glacier vault service no longer accepts new customers; AWS recommends these S3 Glacier classes
  • As of 4 November 2026: minimum durations are from the S3 User Guide
Exam tip

Cheapest long-term archive: S3 Glacier Deep Archive. Archive with instant reads: Instant Retrieval.

S3 Lifecycle and Versioning

  • An S3 Lifecycle configuration holds rules with two actions: transition (move to another storage class) and expiration (delete)
  • Rules apply to existing and new objects, and lower storage costs as data cools
  • S3 Versioning keeps multiple versions of an object: an overwrite adds a version, a delete adds a delete marker
  • You can restore an earlier version after an accidental delete or overwrite
  • Versioning is off by default; once enabled it can only be suspended, and each version is billed

Exam tip

Move or delete data automatically as it ages: a lifecycle policy.

Block Storage: Amazon EBS and Instance Store

Amazon EBS (Elastic Block Store) Instance store
What Block storage volumes attached to EC2, used like a hard drive Temporary block storage on disks attached to the host
Data Persists independently of the instance; replicated within an AZ Deleted when the instance stops, hibernates or terminates
Good for Operating systems, databases, data you keep Buffers, caches, scratch data
Cost Pay for what you provision No extra charge, included in the instance price
  • Snapshots are point-in-time backups of EBS volumes
  • SSD volumes suit transactional work; HDD volumes suit throughput; encryption uses AWS KMS
Exam tip

Disk that survives the instance: EBS. Temporary scratch space: instance store.

3File storage, hybrid, backup and practice

File Storage: Amazon EFS and Amazon FSx

Service What it is Remember
Amazon EFS Serverless, elastic file storage that grows and shrinks automatically; NFS; shared by many EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda and Fargate workloads; Regional (multi-AZ) or One Zone Shared Linux files
Amazon FSx Fully managed file systems in four kinds: Windows File Server (SMB, Active Directory), NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS and Lustre Windows shares or specialist file systems
  • EFS is not supported on Windows-based EC2 instances
Exam tip

Shared Linux file system: EFS. Windows file shares: FSx for Windows File Server.

AWS Storage Gateway: Cloud Storage for On-Premises Apps [Verify live]

  • AWS Storage Gateway connects an on-premises software appliance to cloud storage
  • Run it as a virtual machine or hardware appliance on site, or as an EC2 instance
  • S3 File Gateway: NFS and SMB file shares stored as S3 objects, with local caching for low latency
  • Volume Gateway: iSCSI volumes; cached keeps data in S3 and hot data locally, stored keeps all data local with snapshots in S3
  • Tape Gateway replaces tape libraries; FSx File Gateway is also listed
  • As of 4 November 2026: check the docs for current gateway types

Exam tip

On-premises files or volumes backed by AWS storage with a local cache: Storage Gateway.

AWS Backup and AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery

Service What it does Remember
AWS Backup Centralizes and automates backups across AWS services, such as EC2, EBS, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and FSx; backup plans, tag-based selection, cold storage lifecycle, cross-Region and cross-account copies, Vault Lock (WORM) Back up everything one way
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery Continuously replicates servers, on premises or in the cloud, to a low-cost staging area; launches recovery instances within minutes; drills and fail back Recover fast
Exam tip

Scheduled, policy-based backups: AWS Backup. Fast server recovery after a disaster: Elastic Disaster Recovery.

What the Exam Asks: Storage

  • Object, block or file: S3, EBS or instance store, EFS or FSx
  • Which S3 class: frequent, unknown pattern, infrequent, re-creatable, or archive
  • Lifecycle or versioning: move and delete on a schedule, or keep and restore old versions
  • EBS or instance store: survives the instance, or temporary
  • EFS or FSx: shared Linux files, or Windows shares and specialist systems
  • Storage Gateway: on-premises access backed by AWS storage
  • Backup or Elastic Disaster Recovery: policy-based copies, or fast server recovery
Exam tip

Match access pattern and durability need to the cheapest class that fits.

Design Check: Tidewater's Storage Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
Millions of product photos, served over the internet Amazon S3 (Standard, or Intelligent-Tiering)
Order records kept for years, rarely read S3 Glacier Deep Archive, moved by a lifecycle rule
Recover an accidentally overwritten file S3 Versioning
A fast disk for the database server Amazon EBS volume
Temporary scratch space for image processing Instance store
One set of files shared by the Linux web servers Amazon EFS
Warehouse files kept on site, backed by the cloud AWS Storage Gateway
Consistent backups, and fast recovery of servers AWS Backup and Elastic Disaster Recovery
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

Try It: A Bucket, Versioning and a Lifecycle Rule (Optional)

  • Goal: see versioning and lifecycle rules work in a practice account
  • Create a bucket (the name must be unique) and upload a small text file
  • Turn on versioning, change the file, upload it again, and list the versions
  • Add a lifecycle rule that moves objects to Standard-IA after 30 days and expires them after 365 days
  • Clean up: delete every version, then the bucket

Creates a bucket and turns on versioning (the bucket name is an example)

aws s3 mb s3://tidewater-practice-example --region eu-west-1
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket tidewater-practice-example --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
Exam tip

Hands-on work is not tested on this exam, but it makes the storage classes memorable.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater's customers upload product photos that must be stored durably, at any scale, and served over the internet. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon EBS, with a volume attached to one server
  • BAmazon S3, with the photos stored as objects in a bucket
  • CEC2 instance store, on the disks of the web servers
  • DAmazon EFS, with a shared file system for the servers
Show the answer

Answer: B. Amazon S3 stores any amount of data as objects, durably, and serves it to the internet. EBS and instance store give disks to individual servers, and EFS provides a shared file system rather than object storage.

S2Tidewater keeps order records for seven years, almost never reads them, and can wait hours to retrieve one. Which S3 storage class has the lowest cost for this data?

  • AS3 Standard-IA, which keeps millisecond access
  • BS3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, which reads in milliseconds
  • CS3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves data between tiers
  • DS3 Glacier Deep Archive, which retrieves in hours
Show the answer

Answer: D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for data read less than once a year when hours of retrieval time are acceptable. The other classes cost more because they keep millisecond access or add automatic tiering.

S3Log files are read often for 30 days, rarely after that, and can be deleted after a year. What should Tidewater configure to move and then delete them automatically?

  • AS3 Versioning, which keeps every version of each object
  • BS3 Replication, which copies objects to another Region
  • CAn S3 Lifecycle configuration with transition and expiration actions
  • DAWS Storage Gateway, which caches files on premises
Show the answer

Answer: C. A lifecycle configuration transitions objects to cheaper classes and expires them on a schedule. Versioning keeps old versions, replication copies objects between buckets, and Storage Gateway connects on-premises systems to AWS storage.

S4Tidewater's Linux web servers run on several EC2 instances and must read and write the same set of files at the same time. The storage should grow and shrink automatically. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon EFS, a shared and elastic file system
  • BAmazon EBS, a volume attached to one instance
  • CEC2 instance store, temporary disks on the host
  • DS3 Glacier Deep Archive, a low-cost archive
Show the answer

Answer: A. Amazon EFS is serverless, elastic file storage that many instances can mount at once. An EBS volume serves an instance, instance store is temporary, and Glacier Deep Archive is an archive that cannot be mounted as a file system.

S5Which TWO statements about EC2 instance store and Amazon EBS are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AInstance store volumes are billed separately for every gigabyte stored
  • BData on an instance store volume is deleted when the instance stops or terminates
  • CEBS volumes are attached to the host and are meant for temporary data
  • DAn EBS volume keeps its data independently of the instance it is attached to
  • EEBS snapshots must be kept on the instance store of the same host
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Instance store is temporary, so its data is deleted when the instance stops or terminates, while an EBS volume persists independently of the instance. Instance store is included in the instance price, EBS is the persistent option, and snapshots are stored separately as backups.

S6Tidewater wants one place to define backup schedules and retention for its EC2 volumes, RDS databases and EFS file systems, and to copy backups to another Region. Which service should it use?

  • AAWS Storage Gateway, with a gateway on its premises
  • BAmazon S3 Versioning, with versions of each object
  • CAWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, with replicated servers
  • DAWS Backup, with backup plans and cross-Region copies
Show the answer

Answer: D. AWS Backup centralizes policy-based backups across services and can copy them across Regions. Storage Gateway connects on-premises systems, versioning keeps object versions in one bucket, and Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers for fast recovery.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Types object (S3), block (EBS, instance store) and file (EFS, FSx)
S3 classes Standard for frequent use, Intelligent-Tiering for unknown patterns, IA classes for infrequent use, Glacier classes for archives
Lifecycle and versioning rules transition and expire objects; versions let you restore earlier copies
EBS and instance store a disk that persists, and temporary scratch space
Hybrid and protection Storage Gateway for on-premises access, Backup for policies, Elastic Disaster Recovery for fast recovery
